samples: This program reads a text file, splits it into words, lowercases them, counts how often each word appears, and sorts the results from most frequent to least frequent. Its main entry point prints the top ten words with their counts, using the first command-line argument as the file path or a default sample file if none is provided. It is useful if you want a simple word-frequency report, but it only handles basic space-separated words and does not do advanced tokenization or punctuation cleanup.
